titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Wickedness of Judas (ch. 108)
about: The previous part ended with Christ nailed to the cross; this chapter turns to Judas, whose wickedness it proves from the prophets in a long chain of 'and as X prophesied and said': David (among them Psalms 41 and 109, whose verses John 13:18 and Acts 1:20 apply to Judas), Solomon in Proverbs, Isaiah, Moses in Deuteronomy, Jeremiah and Job (who describe the doom of the wicked and covetous man), Hosea, and Habakkuk. The chain closes on the thirty pieces of silver. The quotations are the author's own fitted wording and some have no match I could find; the notes say where.

sentences.i: Chapter 108: Concerning the wickedness of Judas the perverse
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ 'concerning' governs እከየ, the construct state of እከይ 'evil, wickedness' (the construct state is marked by the final vowel -ä, እከይ → እከየ, which marks 'of'), so እከየ ይሁዳ is 'the wickedness of Judas'. ይሁዳ is the same name as Judah; in this chapter it is Judas, the betrayer, as the thirty silver pieces at the end show. ዕልው is 'perverse, crooked' (from ዐለወ 'be crooked, pervert'), here an adjective after the name; whether it belongs to the name ('Judas the perverse') or to the noun I take it as the former (?). It follows the previous part, which ended on Christ nailed on the cross; the chapter now turns to the betrayer, and its whole method is the chain of citations 'and as X prophesied and said'.

sentences.t: ወበእንተ ፡ እከዩ ፡ ለይሁዳ ፡ ረሲዕ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ በእንቲአሁ ፡ ለብእሲ ፡ ዐማፂ ፡ ይንዕዎ ፡ እኪት ፡ ለአማስኖ ፤
sentences.l: And-concerning wickedness-his for-Judas the-impious prophesied prophets; and-said David concerning-him: 'For-man unjust they-hunt-him(?) evil for-destroying;
sentences.i: And concerning the wickedness of Judas the impious the prophets prophesied; and David said concerning him: 'Evils will hunt the unjust man to destroy him;
sentences.n: Opens the catena. The frame ወበከመ ተነበየ X ወይቤ 'and as X prophesied and said' (ወ- 'and', በ- + ከመ 'as', perfect ተነበየ from the tä-stem of ነበየ 'say, prophesy') will recur all through the chapter; it is flagged here once. በእንቲአሁ 'concerning him' is በእንተ + -አሁ. The quotation is Psalm 140:11 (139:12 in the Greek numbering), 'evil will hunt the unjust man to destruction'. ይንዕዎ is the verb 'hunt, pursue' + -ዎ 'him', but I cannot fix the root in Dillmann with confidence (the same lemma ነዐወ is read 'prevail' (?) elsewhere in this text, so the sense 'hunt' is unsettled), and it is plural-looking before a feminine singular እኪት 'evil', so I take እኪት as a collective, 'evils' (?). ለአማስኖ is ለ- 'for, to' + አማስኖ, the verbal noun of አማሰነ 'destroy', so 'for destroying'. ለብእሲ ዐማፂ: the ለ- here marks the object ('the unjust man'), as in ለኃጥእ below. ረሲዕ 'impious, wicked' qualifies ይሁዳ.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ወይገብእ ፡ ጻማሁ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ርእሱ ፡ ወትወርድ ፡ ዐመፃሁ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ድማሑ ።
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'And-it-will-return toil-his upon head-his, and-it-will-come-down injustice-his upon crown-his.'
sentences.i: And again he said: 'And his toil will return upon his head, and his injustice will come down upon his crown (?).'
sentences.n: Psalm 7:16 (7:17 in some numberings): the wicked man's labour returns on his own head. ወይገብእ is the 3ms imperfect of ገብአ 'return' with ጻማሁ 'his toil' as subject; ትወርድ is the 3fs of ወረደ 'descend', agreeing with ዐመፃሁ 'his injustice' (feminine). ድማሑ I read as 'his crown, top of the head' (?), for the parallel to ርእሱ 'his head'; the word is not secure to me.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ አብድ ፡ ወዐማፂ ፡ የሐውር ፡ ፍናዋተ ፡ ዘኢኮነ ፡ ርቱዓተ ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ ይቀጽብ ፡ በዐይን ፡ ወይዴምር ፡ በእግር ፡ ወይሁብ ፡ ትእምርተ ፡ በቅጽበተ ፡ አጻብዕ ፡ ወበአጽንኖ ፡ ከናፍር ፡ ወዕሉት ፡ ልቡ ፡ ትኄሊ ፡ እኪተ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ጊዜ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Solomon his-son and-said: 'Man foolish and-unjust walks ways which-not-were straight; and-he, he-winks with-eye and-joins(?) with-foot and-gives sign with-blinking-of fingers and-with-pressing-of lips; and-perverse heart-his devises evil at-all time;
sentences.i: And as Solomon his son prophesied, he said: 'A foolish and unjust man walks in ways that are not straight; and he winks with his eye, and signals (?) with his foot, and gives a sign with the flick of his fingers and the pressing of his lips; and his heart, being perverse, devises evil at all times;
sentences.n: Proverbs 6:12–14, the portrait of the worthless man (he winks, signals with foot and fingers, plots evil in a crooked heart), here fitted to Judas. ወልዲ is Bezold's spelling of 'his son' (-ዲ for -ሁ), as in the published parts: Solomon is David's son. የሐውር is 'he walks' (ሖረ); ፍናዋተ 'ways' is an accusative plural; ዘኢኮነ is ዘ 'which' + ኢ- + ኮነ, a 3ms perfect 'was' (singular verb with a plural antecedent), and ርቱዓተ is the plural accusative predicate, 'which were not straight'. ወውእቱሰ is 'and he, for his part' (ውእቱ + the contrastive -ሰ). ይቀጽብ በዐይን 'blinks/winks with the eye' (ቀጸበ, root meaning 'blink, strike' (?)); ቅጽበት is a 'blink, twinkling', hence በቅጽበተ አጻብዕ 'with the flick of fingers' (?). ይዴምር በእግር: ደመረ is 'join, add, gather', so 'joins/gathers (?) with the foot' is the literal sense and 'signals with the foot' in the free translation is a guess from the Proverbs parallel (?). አጽንኖ is 'pressing, making firm' (?), perhaps a verbal noun of አጽንዐ, though the final radical does not match (?). ዕሉት is perhaps the passive participle of ዐለወ 'crooked, perverse' (?), and ልብ 'heart' is here construed as feminine, so ትኄሊ is 3fs 'she devises'.

sentences.t: ዘከመዝ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ያመጽእ ፡ ህከከ ፡ ወቀትለ ፡ ወክዒወ ፡ ደም ፡ በዐመፃ ፡ ወኢያመሥጥ ፡ እምደይን ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ጌጋይ ፡ አውፅኡ ፡ ላዕሌየ ፤
sentences.l: Such-a man brings tumult and-killing and-pouring-out-of blood in-injustice, and-not he-escapes from-judgment. And-as prophesied David father-his and-said: 'A-word-of wrong they-brought-out against-me;
sentences.i: Such a man brings tumult and killing and the shedding of blood by injustice, and he does not escape judgment. And as David his father prophesied, he said: 'They have brought out a word of wrong against me;
sentences.n: Proverbs again (the sense of 6:14–15 (?); the lines before ወበከመ are the author's own comment). ዘከመዝ 'such as this' is ዘ + ከመዝ 'thus'. ህከከ 'tumult, disturbance'; ክዒወ ደም 'the pouring out of blood' (ከዐወ 'pour', here a verbal noun in the construct before ደም). ወኢያመሥጥ is ኢ- 'not' + ያመሥጥ, the 3ms of አመሠጠ 'escape'; እምደይን 'from judgment'. Then David again, now on the betrayal: Psalm 41, with the verses in the English numbering 41:8–9 (40:9–10 in the Greek). ነገረ ጌጋይ is 'a word of wrong' (ጌጋይ is 'fault, sin', not strictly 'falsehood'), አውፅኡ 'they brought out', ላዕሌየ 'against me' (ላዕለ + -የ). The line is the Greek's 'they set an unlawful word against me', so I take አውፅኡ loosely as 'they brought out, uttered' (?).

sentences.t: ዘኖመሰ ፡ ኢይነቅህኑ ፡ እንጋ ፡ ብእሴ ፡ ሰላምየ ፡ ዘኪያሁ ፡ እትአመን ፡ ዘይሴሰይ ፡ እክልየ ፡ አንሥአ ፡ ሰኰናሁ ፡ ላዕሌየ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ አሌሎቱ ፡ ለውእቱ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ዐማፂ ፡ ዘያመጽእ ፡ ለመንሱት ፤
sentences.l: as-for-he-who-slept, will-he-not-wake then(?)? Man-of peace-my, whom him I-trust, he-who-eats food-my, has-raised sole-his against-me; and-as prophesied Isaiah prophet and-said: 'Woe-to-him, to-that man unjust who brings to-mänsut;
sentences.i: As for him who has fallen asleep, will he not wake then (?)? The man of my peace, whom I trusted, who eats my food, has raised his foot against me; and as Isaiah the prophet prophesied, he said: 'Woe to that unjust man who brings (it) to mänsut (?);
sentences.n: Psalm 41:8–9 (English numbering; 40:9–10 in the Greek), the verse Christ himself applies to Judas at the Last Supper (John 13:18). ዘኖመሰ is ዘ 'he who' + ኖመ 'slept' + the contrastive -ሰ ('as for'); ኢይነቅህኑ 'will he not wake?' has the question particle -ኑ; እንጋ is a particle whose sense I cannot fix ('then', 'again', 'still'; the Greek of the Psalm has 'again') (?). ብእሴ ሰላምየ is the construct 'man of my peace', i.e. my friend. ዘኪያሁ እትአመን 'whom I trusted' repeats the pronoun: ዘ- + ኪያ-ሁ, the accusative 'him' (no ብ- 'in'), + እትአመን, the 1s imperfect of ተአመነ 'trust', read as a past. ዘይሴሰይ 'who eats' (ሴሰየ, a quadriliteral, 'eat, take food'); እክል is 'food, grain' and the Psalm's 'bread' is not in the Geʿez. አንሥአ 'he raised'; ሰኰና is 'heel, hoof, sole' (?), the Psalm has 'heel', but l gives 'sole' and i 'foot', the word as written (?). The Isaiah line: the nearest I can match is Isaiah 3:9–11 ('Woe to the wicked'), but I cannot confirm it (?). ለመንሱት is for me an unidentified word, perhaps 'contempt, wretchedness' (?); the sense of the clause is therefore uncertain. አሌሎቱ 'woe to him' (አሌ + ሎቱ), after which ለውእቱ ብእሲ ዐማፂ 'to that unjust man' names the person.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ያአትትዎ ፡ ለኃጥእ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይርአይ ፡ ስብሐተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'Let-them-remove the-sinner so-that-not he-see glory-of God.'
sentences.i: And again he said: 'Let the sinner be removed, so that he not see the glory of God.'
sentences.n: Isaiah 26:10 in the Septuagint form, 'let the wicked be taken away, that he not see the glory of the Lord' (the Hebrew reads differently). ያአትትዎ is the 3mp imperfect (here an optative, 'let them') of አእተተ 'remove, take away' + -ዎ 'him', with ለኃጥእ doubling the object; the plural is impersonal, so 'let the sinner be removed'. ከመ ኢይርአይ 'so that he not see': ከመ with the subjunctive of ርእየ 'see'. ስብሐተ is the accusative of ስብሐት 'glory, praise' in the construct before እግዚኣብሔር.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ይነብብ ፡ ኃጥእ ፡ በዘ ፡ ያስሕት ፡ ርእሶ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ፍርሀተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ቅድመ ፡ አዕይንቲሁ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ፀዋግ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ሀከከ ፡ ያመጽእ ፡ ለህገር ፡ ወያመጽእ ፡ በእንቲአሁ ፡ ተሀጒሎተ ፡ ወዝብጠተ ፡ ወቅጥቃጤ ፡ ዘኢየሐዩ ፡ እስመ ፡ ይትፌሥሕ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ዘይጸልእ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ኢይፈቅድ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይስረይ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ዘያፈደፍድ ፡ በቀለ ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Speaks the-sinner in-that-which he-leads-astray himself, and-there-is-not fear-of God before eyes-his.' And-as prophesied Solomon his-son and-said: 'Base(?) man tumult brings to-the-land, and-brings on-account-of-him destruction and-beating and-breaking which-not he-lives(?), for he-rejoices in-all which he-hates God.' And-as prophesied Moses prophet and-said: 'Not wishes God to-forgive to-him, except that-he increases vengeance upon-him;
sentences.i: And as David the prophet prophesied, he said: 'The sinner speaks in a way that leads himself astray, and there is no fear of God before his eyes.' And as Solomon his son prophesied, he said: 'A base (?) man brings tumult upon the land, and on his account brings destruction and beating and a breaking from which one does not live (?), for he delights in everything that God hates.' And as Moses the prophet prophesied, he said: 'God does not wish to forgive him, but rather increases vengeance upon him;
sentences.n: A long run of three citations, kept whole because it has no ፤ or ። inside it (49 wordspace-separated forms; the build cuts only at the marks). (1) Psalm 36:1–2 (35:2–3 in the Greek): the sinner who deceives himself, and 'no fear of God before his eyes' (the same phrase is Romans 3:18). ያስሕት is the causative አስሕተ 'lead astray' and ርእሶ 'himself' is ርእስ 'head' + -ኦ, the idiom for the reflexive. (2) Solomon: I cannot place this one for certain; it resembles Proverbs 15:27 (the greedy man troubles his house) and Proverbs 6:14, 19 (strife, and what the Lord hates), so the citation is loose (?). ፀዋግ is glossed elsewhere in this text 'wretched, base' (sense uncertain), so I give 'base (?)'; I do not take 'avaricious' from the silver two lines on. ሀከከ 'tumult'; ዝብጠት 'a blow, beating'; ቅጥቃጤ 'breaking'; ዘኢየሐዩ 'which does not live' is cryptic, perhaps 'from which one does not live/recover' (?). እስመ 'for'. ዘይጸልእ እግዚኣብሔር 'that God hates': God is the subject, placed after the verb, not the object. (3) Moses: Deuteronomy 29:20 (29:19 in the Hebrew), 'the Lord will not be willing to forgive him'. ዘእንበለ ዘያፈደፍድ is 'except he who/that increases', hence 'but rather increases'; ያፈደፍድ is the quadriliteral አፈድፈደ 'multiply, add much'; በቀል 'vengeance'.

sentences.t: ወያነብር ፡ መቅሠፍተ ፡ ዲቤሁ ፡ ወይከውን ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፡ ዘጽሑፍ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፡ መርገም ፡ ወይደመሰስ ፡ ስሙ ፡ እምታሕተ ፡ ሰማይ ።
sentences.l: And-he-will-set a-scourge upon-him, and-will-be upon-him that-written in this book, curse, and-will-be-blotted-out name-his from-under heaven.'
sentences.i: and he will set a scourge upon him, and the curse written in this book will be upon him, and his name will be blotted out from under heaven.'
sentences.n: The rest of Deuteronomy 29:20, 'every curse written in this book will cling to him, and the Lord will blot out his name from under heaven'. ወያነብር is 'and he sets' (አንበረ 'set, place'), the subject God; መቅሠፍት 'scourge, plague'. ዘጽሑፍ ... መርገም 'that which is written ... the curse', the noun placed last. ዝንቱ መጽሐፍ 'this book' is Deuteronomy itself, now read by the author as speaking of Judas. ወይደመሰስ is a passive imperfect of ደመሰሰ 'blot out, wipe' (the tä- of the usual passive stem is not written here); እምታሕተ 'from beneath'.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ጥቡዕ ፡ ልቡ ፡ ለቀቲል ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Firm(?) heart-his for-killing;
sentences.i: And as David the prophet prophesied, he said: 'His heart is set (?) on killing;
sentences.n: Probably Psalm 109:16 (108:16 in the Greek), the wicked man who pursued the poor and the broken-hearted 'to put them to death' (Acts 1:20 applies Psalm 109:8 to Judas, and more verses from this psalm follow). Here the line stands alone with ልቡ as the subject. ጥቡዕ I take as 'firm, resolute', 'his heart is set to kill' (?), but it may also be 'broken (heart)', as the Psalm's object, with ለቀቲል 'to be killed/to kill' ('the broken in heart, to kill him'); I cannot decide (?). ለቀቲል is ለ- + the infinitive ቀቲል.

sentences.t: አብደራ ፡ ለመርገም ፡ ወትምጽኦ ፡ አበያ ፡ ለበረከት ፡ ወትርሕቅ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኤርምያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ በእንቲአሁ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ፀዋግ ፡ ይትሀጐል ፡ በእንተ ፡ ፍቅረ ፡ ብሩር ፡ ወይሬኢ ፡ ጽልመተ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጒሕሉቱ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኢዮብ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ በእንቲአሁ ፡ ይዘርዎ ፡ መሠንዮ ፡ ፈጣሪሁ ፡ ወይየብስ ፡ ሥረዊሁ ፡ በታሕቴሁ ፡ ወይትነገፍ ፡ ጽጌ ፡ በመልዕልቴሁ ፡ ወይጠፍእ ፡ እምድር ፡ ዝክሩ ፡ ወይርሕቅ ፡ ስሙ ፡ ነዋኀ ፤
sentences.l: He-hastened(?) to-curse, and-it-comes to-him; he-refused to-blessing, and-it-goes-far from-him.' And-as prophesied Jeremiah prophet concerning-him and-said: 'Man base(?) perishes on-account-of love-of silver, and-sees darkness on-account-of his-craftiness(?).' And-as prophesied Job and-said concerning-him: 'They-scatter-him mäśänyo(?) his-Maker, and-dries-up roots-his beneath-him, and-falls-off flower above-him, and-vanishes from-earth memory-his, and-goes-far name-his far-off;
sentences.i: He was quick (?) to curse, and it comes to him; he refused blessing, and it goes far from him.' And as Jeremiah the prophet prophesied concerning him, he said: 'A base (?) man perishes through love of silver, and sees darkness through his craftiness (?).' And as Job prophesied, he said concerning him: 'They scatter him, his Maker (?), and his roots dry up beneath him, and the blossom above him falls off, and his memory vanishes from the earth, and his name goes far, far away;
sentences.n: The sentence opens on the end of the Psalm 109 passage (109:17 in English, 108:17 in the Greek): 'he loved cursing, and it came upon him; he did not wish blessing, and it was far from him.' አብደራ I cannot identify; 'hastened' is a guess from a root meaning 'hasten' (?), not the Psalm's 'loved', which would suit the parallel better (?); አበያ is አበየ 'refuse', here a verbal noun 'the refusing/he refused' (?), and ለበረከት 'to blessing'; ትምጽኦ 'it comes to him' is the feminine ትመጽእ + -ኦ; ወትርሕቅ 'and it goes far'. The Jeremiah line: a man who perishes for love of silver and sees darkness; I cannot match it to a verse (?), and the attribution may be loose (compare Jeremiah 6:13, all greedy for gain). Judas's silver is the point. ፍቅረ ብሩር 'love of silver' is a construct; ጒሕሉት I read 'craftiness, wiliness' (?). Job 18:15–18 follows: roots dry below, the branch cut off above (18:16), where the Geʿez has 'the flower falls off', memory perishes from the earth (18:17). ይዘርዎ is 3mp 'they scatter him', with ፈጣሪሁ 'his Maker' and the form መሠንዮ in a clause I cannot parse; it may be 'his dwelling' (?) (compare 18:15). ይየብስ 'dries up', ይትነገፍ 'is shaken off, falls', ጽጌ 'flower, blossom', መልዕልቴሁ 'above him', ዝክሩ 'his memory', ነዋኀ 'far, long'.

sentences.t: ወያፈልስዎ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ጽልመት ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይርአይ ፡ ብርሃነ ፡ ለብእሲ ፡ ዐማፂ ፡ ይጠፍእ ፡ ቤቱ ።
sentences.l: and-they-drive-him into darkness so-that-not he-see light, for-man unjust perishes house-his.
sentences.i: and they drive him into darkness, that he not see light; the house of the unjust man perishes.
sentences.n: Job 18:18, 'he is driven from the light into darkness', with ወያፈልስዎ the 3mp of አፈለሰ 'cause to move, drive out' + -ዎ 'him', impersonal 'they drive him'. ከመ ኢይርአይ 'that he not see' is the same final clause as in Isaiah 26:10 above. The last words are ለብእሲ ዐማፂ ይጠፍእ ቤቱ, literally 'to the unjust man, perishes his house', the ለ- naming the owner of the suffixed noun ቤቱ 'his house', here with the owner placed first (compare ስሕተቱ ለአዳም 'Adam's error' in the glossary); compare Job 18:15 and 18:19 (?).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሆሴዕ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ በእንቲአሁ ፡ ስምዑኒ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ጽድቀ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ምሕረተ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ፍርሀተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ልቡ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሐሰት ፡ ወስርቅ ፡ ወቀትል ፡ ወዝሙት ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Hosea and-said concerning-him: 'Hear-me, children-of Israel, for there-is-not righteousness and-there-is-not mercy and-there-is-not fear-of God in heart-his, except falsehood and-theft and-killing and-fornication.'
sentences.i: And as Hosea prophesied, he said concerning him: 'Hear me, children of Israel, for there is no righteousness and no mercy and no fear of God in his heart, except falsehood and theft and killing and fornication.'
sentences.n: Hosea 4:1–2, 'there is no truth, no mercy, no knowledge of God in the land; lying, stealing, killing, adultery'. Note that the author has changed it: where the prophet says 'in the land', the text has ውስተ ልቡ 'in his heart' (singular), applying the list to Judas. ስምዑኒ is ስምዑ 'hear (pl)' + the object suffix -ኒ 'me'. ደቂቀ is the construct plural 'children of'. አልቦ 'there is not'; ዘእንበለ 'except'. ምሕረት 'mercy'. Hosea's 'truth' is here ጽድቅ 'righteousness', and his 'knowledge of God' has become ፍርሀተ እግዚኣብሔር 'fear of God'; the Greek also has 'knowledge', so this is the author's change, or his text's (?). ዝሙት is 'fornication' (Hosea has 'adultery').

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ሰይጣን ፡ ይቁም ፡ በየማኑ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Satan let-him-stand at-right-his;
sentences.i: And as David the prophet prophesied, he said: 'Let Satan stand at his right hand;
sentences.n: Psalm 109:6 (108:6 in the Greek), 'let an accuser/Satan stand at his right hand', a verse of the psalm from which Acts 1:20 takes 109:8 for Judas; whether this verse was applied to Judas too I do not know (?). ይቁም is the jussive of ቆመ 'stand'; በየማኑ 'at his right' is በ- + የማን 'right (hand)' + -ሁ.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ወሢመቶሂ ፡ ይንሣእ ፡ ባዕድ ፡ ወሙሴኒ ፡ ረገመ ፡ በሕግ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ርጉም ፡ ለይኩን ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘይነሣእ ፡ ሕልያነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይቅትል ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሐ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'And-office-his-also let-take another; and-Moses-also cursed in-law and-said: Cursed let-be everyone who-takes bribes(?) in-order-that he-kill blood innocent;
sentences.i: And again he said: 'And let another take his office also; and Moses also cursed in the law, and said: Let everyone be cursed who takes bribes (?) to kill a person of innocent blood;
sentences.n: Psalm 109:8 (108:8 in the Greek), 'his office let another take', the verse Peter quotes of Judas at Acts 1:20. ሢመቶሂ is ሢመት 'office, appointment' + -ሁ 'his' + -ሂ 'also, and'; ይንሣእ 'let him take' (jussive of ነሥአ); ባዕድ 'another, a stranger'. ሙሴኒ is 'Moses also', with -ኒ 'also'. ረገመ በሕግ 'cursed in the law'. Deuteronomy 27:25, 'cursed be he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent person'. ርጉም ለይኩን 'let him be cursed' (ርጉም 'cursed' + ለይኩን the jussive 'let him be'); ሕልያን is, I believe, 'gift, bribe' (?); ከመ ይቅትል ደመ ንጹሐ 'that he kill innocent blood' (an idiom for killing an innocent person; ንጹሕ 'pure, innocent', accusative ንጹሐ).

sentences.i: and let all the people say: Amen and Amen.'
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:25–26, where all the people answer 'Amen' to the curses; the doubled 'Amen and Amen' is the liturgical form. ወይበል is 'and let (him/them) say', the jussive of ብህለ 'say' (the root of ይቤ 'he said'); ሕዝብ 'people' takes a singular verb.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ እንባቆም ፡ ነቢይ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ መኰንንኒ ፡ አለበወ ፡ በእንተዝ ፡ ዕልወተ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ወኢይወፅእ ፡ ፍትሐ ፡ ጽድቅ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኃጥእ ፡ ይትዔገሎ ፡ ለጻድቅ ፡ በእንተዝ ፡ ይወፅእ ፡ ፍትሕ ፡ ግፍቱእ ።
sentences.l: And-again prophesied Habakkuk prophet while he-says: 'And-the-governor he-has-confounded(?), therefore perversion-of law, and-not goes-out judgment-of righteousness, for the-sinner besets the-righteous; therefore goes-out judgment perverted.'
sentences.i: And again Habakkuk the prophet prophesied, saying: 'And the ruler has been confounded (?); therefore the law is perverted, and no righteous judgment goes out, for the sinner besets (?) the righteous; therefore perverted (?) judgment goes out.'
sentences.n: Habakkuk 1:3–4: the law is slack, judgment never goes out, the wicked surround the righteous, so judgment goes out crooked. እንዘ ይብል 'while he says' (the frame for a quotation; compare ch. 107). መኰንንኒ is መኰንን 'governor, judge' + -ኒ 'and, also'; አለበወ I cannot fix: I cannot confirm the sense of a root ለበወ in Dillmann, nor whether አ- is causative here, so 'the ruler has been confounded' is only a guess (?). በእንተዝ 'therefore' is በእንተ + ዝ 'this'. ዕልወተ ሕግ 'perversion of the law' is a construct chain with no verb, 'the law is perverted'. ፍትሐ ጽድቅ 'judgment of righteousness' (ፍትሕ 'judgment'; accusative in form though it is the subject of ኢይወፅእ 'does not go out', a case I do not explain (?)). ይትዔገሎ I read as 'besets him', as a tä-stem of a root meaning 'surround' (compare ዐገተ 'besiege' elsewhere in this text), the exact root uncertain, with ለጻድቅ doubling the object (?). ግፍቱእ is 'perverted, oppressed' (?). Habakkuk was already named in ch. 106 and ch. 107 (Habakkuk 3:4, the horns).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ይሬኢ ፡ ኃጥእ ፡ ወይትመዐዕ ፡ ወየሐቂ ፡ ስነኒሁ ፡ ወይትመሰው ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Sees the-sinner and-is-angry, and-gnashes teeth-his and-melts.'
sentences.i: And as David the prophet prophesied, he said: 'The sinner sees and is angry, and gnashes his teeth and melts.'
sentences.n: Psalm 112:10 (111:10 in the Greek), 'the wicked sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and melts away'. ይትመዐዕ is 'be angry' (ተመዐዐ); የሐቂ 'he gnashes' (the root is not clear to me, I take it from the sense (?)); ስነኒሁ 'his teeth'; ይትመሰው 'melts, dissolves' (ተመሰወ).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ጽሉእ ፡ በኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ መዳልወ ፡ ዐመፃ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኤርምያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ድልው ፡ ሊተ ፡ ዐስብየ ፡ ፴ ፡ ብሩር ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Solomon his-son and-said: 'Hated before God scales-of injustice.' And-as prophesied Jeremiah prophet and-said: 'Concerning Judas ready for-me my-wage, thirty silver.' * * * * * * * * *
sentences.i: And as Solomon his son prophesied, he said: 'The scales of injustice are hated before God.' And as Jeremiah the prophet prophesied, he said: 'Concerning Judas, my wage is ready for me: thirty (pieces) of silver.'
sentences.n: Proverbs 11:1 (also 20:23), 'a false balance is an abomination to the Lord'. ጽሉእ 'hated, abominable'; በኀበ 'before, in the sight of'; መዳልው is 'scales, balance' (from ደለወ 'weigh'), so መዳልወ ዐመፃ is 'scales of injustice'. The chapter closes with the citation that Matthew 27:9–10 gives to Jeremiah, the thirty silver pieces paid to Judas (in the Hebrew prophets the passage is Zechariah 11:12–13; the text, like Matthew, names Jeremiah). ድልው 'ready, prepared'; ሊተ 'to me'; ዐስብ is 'wage, price' + -የ 'my'. ፴ is the numeral 30, in speech ሠላሳ (śälasa) 'thirty' (?, the usual spoken form, as in the glossary). ብሩር 'silver'. The final ፨ ፨ ... run belongs to this unit; the unit has no closing ። because the text ends at the paragraph mark.
